title: Kansas Birth Justice Society official site

title: Liberation Place ICT public hub

title: Iowa City Mutual Aid current first-party site

data.notes: Current 2026 first-party site documents direct aid, encampment support, community meals, a community garden/fridge, prison-support work and Mutual Aid 101. Its own newsletter repeatedly solicits anti-capitalist and abolitionist work, explicitly accepts anarchist submissions, and carries recurring 'Ask an Anarchist' content. This is explicit anarchist-associated publishing activity, not a claim that the organization self-identifies as anarchist. The site advertises Instagram but the exact organization handle was not safely resolved in this bounded pass.

title: Autonomy Iowa City about page

data.notes: First-party about page says Autonomy Iowa City was established in 2022, originally as the Iowa City Jane Collective, by reproductive-justice activists and care workers, and organizes a support network for abortion and gender-affirming hormone care. Iowa City Mutual Aid's current 2026 publication repeatedly features Autonomy Iowa City as an ongoing local project/partner surface.

title: Great Plains Action Society official site

data.notes: Current first-party site describes GPAS as an Indigenous-led grassroots nonprofit working across Iowa and Eastern Nebraska using mutual-aid efforts, non-violent direct action, land defense and solidarity. Iowa City Mutual Aid's current 2026 site documents garden processing and propane-storage collaboration at GPAS.

title: Corridor Community Action Network official site

data.notes: Current first-party site says CCAN began in 2019 and developed into a social-justice network connecting organizations across Iowa's Corridor for mutual support, calls to action, food security, harm reduction, immigrant aid, tenants' rights and workers' justice. A current 2026 public event identifies CCAN-Con in downtown Iowa City as focused on advocacy, mutual aid and grassroots organizing.

title: Area-code-hunt shard B: 313, 316, 319
summary: Bounded dedicated shard-B area-code organization enumeration over Detroit, Wichita and Iowa City/eastern Iowa. Nine distinct organization identities were materialized with separate investigation targets, current-status controls, historical Food Not Bombs continuity limits, one program relation and one current collaboration relation. No individual political affiliation or violent-conduct claim is inferred.

data.research_question: Which public organizations matching or closely adjacent to the requested anarchist, anti-authoritarian, autonomous, Food Not Bombs, mutual-aid and organization-network seed families can be defensibly enumerated from shard-B area codes 313, 316 and 319?
data.method: Dedicated area-code-hunt-v1-expanded pass using the current NANPA in-service U.S. geographic-area-code surface and deterministic npa mod 3 sharding; literal code searches for anarchists, anarchist collective, anarchist black cross, Food Not Bombs and mutual aid plus Detroit, Wichita and Iowa City/eastern-Iowa locality searches; first-party organization sites, public Linktree, historical Food Not Bombs directories, current search engines, public Reddit discovery and repository-wide dedupe. Black Rose/Rosa Negra, Anarchist Black Cross and Food Not Bombs seed-family surfaces were re-checked for these localities rather than assumed current. Historical directories were discovery seeds only. X and Reddit official APIs were not used.
classification_rules: Only current authoritative in-service U.S. geographic NPAs are eligible seeds; shard B is npa mod 3 == 1.
Completed codes through 310 were not repeated.
Historical directories and old public handles do not establish current status.
Organizations retain their own first-party self-description; abolitionist, reproductive-justice, mutual-aid, Indigenous-led and social-justice-network identities are not silently relabeled anarchist.
Explicit anarchist-associated publishing is recorded separately from organizational self-identification.
No individual political affiliation or violent conduct is inferred.
Name or handle similarity alone never merges organizations.

findings.notes: Detroit Peer Respite is current first-party abolitionist mutual aid; Eastside Mutual Aid is current first-party direct-action mutual aid; Detroit Food Not Bombs remains historical/current-status unresolved.
KBJS is current Wichita-founded reproductive-justice organization explicitly providing mutual aid; Liberation Place is its distinct current public-facing mutual-aid hub.

ICMA is highly current and explicitly publishes anti-capitalist, abolitionist and anarchist-associated material without being relabeled anarchist; Autonomy, GPAS and CCAN are current first-party organizations; Iowa City Food Not Bombs is historical/current-status unresolved.

findings.uncertainty: The historical Detroit FNB Facebook endpoint is not assumed current; @esmutualaid is current public discovery but still needs first-party endpoint resolution. First-party sites additionally expose Instagram/Facebook/Twitter or mailing-list surfaces whose exact account URLs were not safely resolved in this bounded pass.
